Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 55, verses 1–13:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Rahman (the Most Merciful): a name among the names of God, exalted is He.

ʿAllama al-Qur'an (taught the Qur'an): that is, He taught the Qur'an to whomever of His servants He willed.

Khalaqa al-insan (created man): Adam, and likewise his descendants.

ʿAllamahu al-bayan (taught him eloquence): that is, He taught Adam al-bayan (clear expression), which is speech and the ability to express what is in the self in whatever language. All of this is the teaching of God, mighty and majestic; had it not been for God, no human would have spoken.

Al-shams wa al-qamar bi-husban (the sun and the moon run by a reckoning): that is, they run by a known calculation, measured in their zodiacal mansions and their stations.

Wa al-najm wa al-shajar yasjudan (the star and the tree prostrate): al-najm is that which has no stem among plants, and al-shajar is that which has a stem. They both prostrate, submitting to God in whatever He wills of them, in obedience, like the prostration of the responsible beings (al-mukallafun).

Wa al-sama' rafaʿaha (and the heaven He raised): that is, above the earth and high above it.

Wa wada'a al-mizan (and He set up the balance): that is, He established justice among the servants, commanded it, and inspired them to make the instruments of it.

Alla tatghaw fi al-mizan (that you not transgress in the balance): that is, so that you do not act unjustly in the balance, which is what is weighed with instruments.

Wa aqimu al-wazn bi-al-qist (and establish the weight with justice): that is, do not diminish what you weigh; rather, give it in full.

Wa al-ardha wada'aha lil-anam (and the earth He set down for the creatures): that is, He fixed it and spread it out, just as He raised the heaven and made it high, for the creatures to live upon it, namely humankind, jinn, animals, and every living being.

Fiha fakiha wa al-nakhl dhat al-akmam (in it are fruits and palm trees with sheaths): that is, in the earth are fruits, meaning everything humans enjoy eating of the many kinds of fruit; and the palm trees with sheaths, which are the containers of their spathes (tal').

Wa al-habb dhu al-ʿasf (and grain with its husk): that is, and in the earth is grain of wheat and barley, and its ʿasf is its chaff.

Wa al-rayhan (and fragrant plants): a well-known plant, and what is meant is the varieties of fragrant, sweet-smelling herbs.

Fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban (so which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?): that is, which of the blessings of your Lord, O company of jinn and humankind, will you deny? They are many and cannot be counted or enumerated. The answer is: "We deny nothing of Your blessings, our Lord; to You be praise."

Meaning of the verses:

God, exalted is He, says, "al-Rahman ʿallama al-Qur'an" (The Most Merciful taught the Qur'an): He informs that He is the Merciful who taught His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) the Qur'an, not as the deniers claim, that a human taught it. The Merciful whose mercy encompasses all things, and it is manifest and evident in the favors and blessings He enumerates. Among them is His creation of man, Adam and his descendants, and His teaching them al-bayan, which is speech and clear expression of what is in their souls. "Al-shams wa al-qamar bi-husban" (The sun and the moon run by a reckoning): they run to benefit people in knowing the times of their worship and the due dates of their debts, and these are manifestations of mercy. "Wa al-najm wa al-shajar yasjudan" (The star and the tree prostrate): the star is food for your livestock, and the tree bears your fruit and some of your food. "Yasjudan" (they prostrate): in submission to God in what He wills of them; they do not disobey as the two weighty ones (humans and jinn) disobey. "Wa al-sama' rafaʿaha ʿan al-ardh" (And the heaven He raised above the earth): He did not stick it to the earth, as a favor to the two weighty ones in raising it and adorning it with its stars, sun, and moon. "Wa wada'a al-mizan" (And He set up the balance): that is, justice, where He commanded it and inspired the making of its instruments, and implanted its love and desire in souls, so that "alla tatghaw fi al-mizan" (you not transgress in the balance). "Wa aqimu al-wazn bi-al-qist" (And establish the weight with justice): with fairness. "Wa la tukhsiru al-mizan" (And do not make the balance deficient): that is, do not diminish it when you weigh; rather, give it in full. All of this is a favor and a variety of the mercies of the Merciful.

"Wa al-ardha wada'aha lil-anam" (And the earth He set down for the creatures): that is, He fixed it, lowered it, and spread it out for the living of the creatures, namely humankind, jinn, and animals. "Fiha fakiha wa al-nakhl dhat al-akmam" (In it are fruits and palm trees with sheaths): that is, the containers of the spathe; and the grain, wheat and barley, with its husk, that is the chaff; and the fragrant plants. These are kinds of food for humans and animals: food, fruit, and fragrant plants. All of these are manifestations of the mercy that the Merciful has poured out. "Fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma" (So which of the favors of your Lord), O company of jinn and humankind, "tukadhdhiban" (will you deny?). We deny nothing of Your blessings, our Lord; to You be praise.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Al-Rahman, like the name of Allah, may not be applied to anyone other than the Lord, blessed and exalted is He. One may say "so-and-so is ʿaziz (mighty), raḥim (merciful), ʿalim (knowing), or hakim (wise)," but one may not say "Rahman," just as one may not say "Ilah," "al-Ilah," or "Allah."

2- It is related in the Sahih, concerning the virtue of learning the Qur'an, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best of you is the one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it."

3- The obligation of establishing justice and enjoining it upon one another, and of monitoring the scales of merchants and correcting their faults.

4- The obligation to thank God for His favors.

5- The recommendation to say "We deny nothing of Your blessings, our Lord; to You be praise" when hearing the recitation of "Fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban."

6- The legitimacy of learning astronomy for determining the qibla and the times of prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage.

1- Al-Rahman, like the name of Allah, may not be applied to anyone other than the Lord, blessed and exalted is He. One may say "so-and-so is ʿaziz (mighty), raḥim (merciful), ʿalim (knowing), or hakim (wise)," but one may not say "Rahman," just as one may not say "Ilah," "al-Ilah," or "Allah."

2- It is related in the Sahih, concerning the virtue of learning the Qur'an, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best of you is the one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it."

3- The obligation of establishing justice and enjoining it upon one another, and of monitoring the scales of merchants and correcting their faults.

4- The obligation to thank God for His favors.

5- The recommendation to say "We deny nothing of Your blessings, our Lord; to You be praise" when hearing the recitation of "Fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban."

6- The legitimacy of learning astronomy for determining the qibla and the times of prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 55, verses 14–25:

Explanation of the words:

﻿﻿"Khalaqa al-insana min salsalin kal-fakhkhar" (He created man from clay like pottery): that is, He created Adam from dry clay that makes a ringing sound like pottery, which is clay that has been baked.

"Wa khalaqa al-jann min marijin min nar" (And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire): that is, He created the father of the jinn from pure flame of fire, free of smoke, mixed with red, blue and yellow.

"Rabbu al-mashriqayni wa rabbu al-maghribayn" (Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests): that is, the east of winter and the east of summer, meaning the places where the sun rises in each of them. Likewise the two wests, in summer and in winter.

"Maraja al-bahrayni yaltaqiyan" (He released the two seas, meeting each other): that is, He let loose the two seas, the fresh and the salt, so that they meet, as seen by the eye.

"Baynahuma barzakhun la yabghiyan" (Between them is a barrier they do not transgress): that is, between them is a barrier, so that neither overpowers the other and mixes with it.

"Yakhruju minhuma al-lu'lu'u wal-marjan" (From both come forth pearls and coral): that is, from the combined waters, the one that is sweet and the one that is salt, there come forth pearls and coral, which is beads of red, and is the small pearls.

"Wa lahu al-jawari al-munsha'atu fi al-bahri kal-a'lam" (And His are the ships sailing in the sea, like mountains): that is, the ships created to move in the sea, tall like mountains in size and height.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention what the Most Merciful, majestic is His majesty, has poured out of His mercy, which encompasses everything, of blessings and favours that cannot be counted, enumerated or limited. So He, exalted, says: ﴿He created man﴾, that is, the Most Merciful whom the deniers ignored, saying: "And what is the Most Merciful?" The Most Merciful who created man, Adam, the first human He created, and from what He created him: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾, that is, from clay with a ringing and sound. ﴿Like pottery﴾. He created man, and He created the jinn, a world like the world of man; He created their origin from smokeless fire, which is the flame of fire mixed together. So which of the blessings of your Lord will you two deny, O company of jinn and mankind? These are blessings that exceed the count of man. Who is the Lord of the two easts and the Lord of the two wests? Who created them, owns them, and subjected them for the benefit of man? It is the Most Merciful. So which of your Lord's blessings will you deny? We deny none of Your blessings, our Lord; to You be praise. The Most Merciful released the two seas, the salt and the fresh, sending them upon each other so that they mingle. It is as if they have mixed when He placed between them a barrier, so they do not transgress, and one does not mix with the other. So which of your Lord's blessings will you deny? He brings forth from them pearls and coral: He who created in the combined seas pearls and coral, which are beads of white, red and green. For whose benefit did the Most Merciful create them? It is for the benefit of man; they are therefore a blessing and a mercy from the mercies of the Most Merciful. ﴿So which of the blessings of your Lord will you deny?﴾ ﴿And His are the ships﴾, that is, to the Most Merciful belong the ships sailing in the sea, the made and constructed vessels in the sea, in the hulls of ships, like mountains in their height and elevation, appearing on the sea as mountains appear on land, for the benefit of those whom the Most Merciful created for the benefit of man. They are therefore the mercy of the Most Merciful and His favour upon man. So which of your Lord's blessings, O company of mankind and jinn, will you deny? Acknowledge, confess, and give thanks to the Most Merciful.

3- Knowledge of the craft of pearls and coral, and of the ships which are on the sea like mountains in height and prominence.

**Explanation of the Words (Sharh al-Kalimat):**

*Kullu man 'alayha fan*: That is, everyone upon the earth, whether human, animal or jinn, is perishing, i.e., destined to die.

*Wa yabqa wajhu rabbika*: That is, His Self (dhat) and Face, glorified and exalted is He.

*Dhu al-jalali wa al-ikram*: That is, the Majesty and the Bestowal of favours upon His servants in general and upon the believers in particular.

*Yas'aluhu man fi as-samawati wa al-ard*: That is, they ask Him for their needs upon which their lives depend, such as provision and the strength to worship, forgiveness of sins, and honour from the Lord.

*Kulla yawmin huwa fi sha'n*: That is, every moment He is engaged in affairs which He manifests according to His decree: He raises up peoples and abases others.

*Sanafrughu lakum ayyuha ath-thaqalan*: That is, for your reckoning and recompense after the end of this worldly life, and We shall repay each according to what he did.

*In astatum an tanfudhu*: That is, if you are able to get out.

*Min aqtari as-samawati wa al-ard*: That is, from the regions of the heavens and the earth.

*Fa-nfudhu la tanfudhuna illa bi-sultan*: That is, then get out. You will not get out except by force, and you have no force; this is a challenge to them to show their inability.

*Yursalu 'alaykuma shuwazun min nar*: That is, a pure flame of fire without smoke.

*Wa nuhasun*: That is, smoke without flame, and it is not far-fetched that it is molten brass.

*Fa-la tantasirani*: That is, you will not be able to resist being driven to the gathering place (al-mahshar).

**Meaning of the Verses (Ma'na al-Ayat):**

The noble context continues to mention the favours of the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. The Mighty and Majestic has said: ﴿Everyone upon it is passing away﴾: everyone on the earth, whether human, jinn, living being or animal, is perishing, leaving neither spirit nor essence. ﴿But there remains the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾, living and never dying, while humans and jinn die. So which of the bounties of your Lord would you deny? Is it the bounty of bringing you into existence and sustaining you with provision and good throughout life? Or the bounty of ending your toils and burdens? Or of destroying your enemies and bringing you near to the everlasting bliss in the Gardens of Bliss? Say, "We deny none of Your bounties, our Lord, and to You belongs all praise."

His saying ﴿He is asked by whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ means they seek Him, by tongue of speech or by state of need, for what they have no independence from: whatever preserves their existence and forgives their sins. His saying ﴿Every day He is in some affair﴾ means the age is never empty of His decree: He governs the affairs of the heavens and the earth, raising some peoples and abasing others.

The saying of the Most Merciful ﴿We shall soon attend to you, O two worlds﴾, meaning humans and jinn: We shall call you to account and recompense the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil and loss. This is the Day when you two shall stand before the Most Merciful, barefoot and naked, and stand before Him for judgment and decision between you. So which of your Lord's bounties would you deny? Is it the justice of His judgment between you, or the making happy of your righteous and the wretchedness of your criminals?

The saying of the Most Merciful: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., to get out, ﴿from their regions and their borders﴾, ﴿then pass through; you will not pass except by a mighty, prevailing force, and you have no power or authority.﴾ Thus does the Most Merciful challenge them while they are driven to the court of final judgment. So which of your Lord's bounties would you deny? Is it the bounty of reviving you after your death, or the bounty of honouring your righteous and humiliating your corrupt, which is justice, where neither mercy nor blessing in the worldly life is equal to them?

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 55, verse 37–45:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Then when the sky splits open﴾: That is, it opens up with gates for the descent of the angels to the earth, to drive creation to the place of gathering (al-mahshar).

﴿And it becomes red like red leather⁠—﴾: That is, the sky becomes reddened like red tanned leather or a red horse, and it melts and becomes like oil-dregs (al-dihan) in its clarity and its melting.

﴿So on that Day, neither humankind nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾: That is, on the Day they come forth from their graves, they will not be asked about their sins, because of the signs they have, such as the blackening and whitening of faces; they will be questioned at the reckoning.

﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾: That is, by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes.

﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾: That is, the forelock of the criminal is joined to his feet, and he is seized and cast into Hell.

﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny﴾: That is, it will be said to them as rebuke and reproach: this is Hell, which the criminals denied in the world.

﴿The criminals⁠﴾: That is, those who committed crimes against themselves through polytheism and sins.

﴿They will circulate between it and scalding, boiling water﴾: That is, they will run back and forth between it and water that is hot, its heat having reached a limit beyond which there is no increase; this is the scalding water (al-hamim al-an). They are given it to drink when they are thirsty and cry out, seeking water to quench their parched thirst.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to present the states of the Resurrection and the terrors of the standing place. So the Glorious and Mighty One said: ﴿Then when the sky splits open﴾, that is, it opens up for the descent of the angels, becoming gates, after it has turned red and its blueness has changed to a redness like the redness of red leather, or a red horse, or a red rose; all of this is apt as a comparison for its color. And it melts and becomes like oil-dregs, as its description came in Surah al-Ma'arij: "On the Day the sky will be like molten brass" (al-muhl), which is the sediment and dregs of oil. ﴿So on that Day﴾, that is, on the day when this happens, distress will intensify, calamity will grow severe, and people will come out of their graves. ﴿Neither humankind nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾, that is, neither human nor jinn. ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?﴾

As for His statement, ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, that is, by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes. ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾, that is, the angel appointed for this will gather the criminal, human or jinn, binding his forelock and his feet together, seize him, and hurl him into the fire of Hell. ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?⁠﴾ Is it the favor of justice, or the favor of honoring the righteous God-fearing ones? Say: "We deny none of Your blessings, our Lord, so to You be praise."

As for His statement, ﴿This is Hell﴾, that is, it will be said to them as rebuke and reproach: this is Hell, which the criminals denied against themselves through polytheism and sins in the worldly life. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They will circulate﴾, that is, they will run back and forth ﴿between it and scalding, boiling water﴾, that is, hot water whose heat has intensified to a limit beyond which there is no increase; they are given it to drink when they cry out from thirst. ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?⁠﴾ Indeed, the disgrace and torment of the criminals is a blessing that human nature recognizes, and none can appreciate it except one who has tasted the fear and the torment which the criminals inflict upon the God-fearing. Therefore their punishment on the Day of Resurrection is a blessing, just as this portrayal of the states and terrors of the Day of Resurrection is a blessing, for by it the believers believed and the God-fearing became God-fearing. Hence, after describing the condition of the people of the Fire, He said: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?⁠﴾

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the cosmic upheaval and the ruin of the world for the Resurrection.
2- People will be raised from their graves with marks that distinguish them, so the fortunate and the wretched are recognized.
3- Condemnation of criminality, which is polytheism, injustice, and sins.

﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾: That is, by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes.

﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾: That is, the forelock of the criminal is joined to his feet, and he is seized and cast into Hell.

﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny﴾: That is, it will be said to them as rebuke and reproach: this is Hell, which the criminals denied in the world.

﴿The criminals⁠﴾: That is, those who committed crimes against themselves through polytheism and sins.

﴿They will circulate between it and scalding, boiling water﴾: That is, they will run back and forth between it and water that is hot, its heat having reached a limit beyond which there is no increase; this is the scalding water (al-hamim al-an). Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to present the states of the Resurrection and the terrors of the standing place. So the Glorious and Mighty One said: ﴿Then when the sky splits open﴾, that is, it opens up for the descent of the angels, becoming gates, after it has turned red and its blueness has changed to a redness like the redness of red leather, or a red horse, or a red rose; all of this is apt as a comparison for its color. And it melts and becomes like oil-dregs, as its description came in Surah al-Ma'arij: "On the Day the sky will be like molten brass" (al-muhl), which is the sediment and dregs of oil. ﴿So on that Day﴾, that is, on the day when this happens, distress will intensify, calamity will grow severe, and people will come out of their graves. ﴿Neither humankind nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾, that is, neither human nor jinn. ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?﴾

As for His statement, ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, that is, by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes. ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾, that is, the angel appointed for this will gather the criminal, human or jinn, binding his forelock and his feet together, seize him, and hurl him into the fire of Hell. ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?⁠﴾ Is it the favor of justice, or the favor of honoring the righteous God-fearing ones? Say: "We deny none of Your blessings, our Lord, so to You be praise."

As for His statement, ﴿This is Hell﴾, that is, it will be said to them as rebuke and reproach: this is Hell, which the criminals denied against themselves through polytheism and sins in the worldly life. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They will circulate﴾, that is, they will run back and forth ﴿between it and scalding, boiling water﴾, that is, hot water whose heat has intensified to a limit beyond which there is no increase; they are given it to drink when they cry out from thirst. ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?⁠﴾ Indeed, the disgrace and torment of the criminals is a blessing that human nature recognizes, and none can appreciate it except one who has tasted the fear and the torment which the criminals inflict upon the God-fearing. Therefore their punishment on the Day of Resurrection is a blessing, just as this portrayal of the states and terrors of the Day of Resurrection is a blessing, for by it the believers believed and the God-fearing became God-fearing. Hence, after describing the condition of the people of the Fire, He said: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?⁠﴾

1- Explanation of the cosmic upheaval and the ruin of the world for the Resurrection.
2- People will be raised from their graves with marks that distinguish them, so the fortunate and the wretched are recognized.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 55, verses 62–78:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Min dunihima jannatan﴾ (and besides these two): i.e., and besides those two gardens there are two other gardens for those who fear the standing before their Lord.

Mudhammatan (dark green): i.e., blackish from the intensity of their greenness.

Fihima ʿaynani naddakhatan (in them two gushing springs): i.e., two fountains constantly and perpetually gushing forth with sweet, pure water.

Fihinna khayratun hisan (in them are good, beautiful women): i.e., in the four gardens are women of good character and beautiful faces.

Hur (maidens with wide, lustrous eyes): i.e., those good women are ḥūr, meaning white; the singular is ḥawrāʾ, meaning white.

Maqṣurat fi al-khiyam (secluded in pavilions): i.e., concealed and kept within their husbands' pavilions. The pavilion (khayma) is of hollow pearl, and it is attributed to palaces (quṣūr). The length of a single pavilion is sixty miles.

Lam yatmithunna insun qablahum wa-la jann (no man or jinn has touched them before them): i.e., no one has had intercourse with them, thereby deflowering them, before their husbands in Paradise.

ʿAla rafrafin khuḍr (on green cushions): i.e., on cushions or carpets; the singular of rafraf is rafrafa, and khuḍr is the plural of akhḍar.

Wa-ʿabqariyyin ḥisan (and beautiful rugs): i.e., ṭanāfis, the plural of ṭunfusa, a carpet with a fine nap; i.e., beautiful carpets.

Tabāraka ism rabbika (blessed is the name of your Lord): i.e., sanctified, and abundant in blessing is the name of your Lord, the Most Merciful.

Dhī al-jalāli wa-al-ikrām (Possessor of majesty and honour): i.e., possessor of greatness and of honour toward His friends and kindness toward His servants.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention Allah's favour and bounty upon His servants, saying: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾, i.e., besides those two gardens there are two other gardens for those among the foremost who fear the standing before their Lord, and these two are for those among the companions of the right who fear the standing before their Lord, though it may also be the reverse; Allah knows best which of the two gardens is better. O Allah, grant us whatever You will of them, for we are content with Your giving, thankful and praising You. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? i.e., which of His bounties and graces would you deny?

And His saying: ﴿Mudhammatan﴾, i.e., green to the point of blackness, for when the greenness of a thing intensifies it inclines toward black; it is said of them that they are mudhammatan. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? i.e., which of His blessings would you deny, O company of jinn and humankind?

﴿In them﴾, i.e., in the two gardens, ﴿are two gushing springs﴾, i.e., two fountains of water constantly and perpetually. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? i.e., which of His grace and kindness would you deny?

And the saying of the Most Merciful: ﴿In them﴾, i.e., in the two gardens, are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates. The word "fruit" may encompass palm and pomegranate, but the mention of palm and pomegranate is for added excellence, like the mention of the middle prayer after the mention of the five prayers in His saying: ﴿Guard over the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 238]. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ We deny nothing of the favours of our Lord; to You belongs all praise.

And His saying: ﴿In them are good, beautiful women﴾, i.e., in the two gardens are their women, good (khayrat, the plural of khayira), of good character and beautiful faces. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? Would you deny such a bounty and honour upon the friends of the Most Merciful?

﴿Maidens secluded in pavilions﴾: those good women are ḥūr, the plural of ḥawrāʾ, meaning white; a ḥawrāʾ is one in whom the whiteness of the eyes overcomes their blackness, which is a feature of feminine beauty. They are kept within pavilions and look at no one but their husbands. The pavilion is of hollow pearl, sixty miles long, attributed to their palaces.

And His saying: ﴿No man or jinn has touched them before them﴾, i.e., no man or jinn has had intercourse with them, deflowering them, before their husbands in Paradise. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? The answer: we deny nothing of the favours of our Lord; to You belongs all praise.

And His saying: ﴿Reclining on green cushions and beautiful carpets﴾, i.e., reclining on green cushions, the singular of rafraf being rafrafa, that is, on green pillows or carpets, and beautiful carpets, i.e., on rugs with a fine nap. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny: the blessings of this world, or of the barzakh, or of the Hereafter? We deny nothing of the favours of our Lord.

And His saying: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of majesty and honour﴾, i.e., blessed is the name of your Lord: sanctified, and abundant in blessings is the name of your Lord, the Most Merciful, Possessor of majesty, i.e., greatness, and of honour toward His friends and righteous servants.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification that the bliss of the Hereafter is greater and more majestic than the bounties of this world.

2- The excellence of dates and pomegranates, so let us investigate their benefits, for truth is the daughter of inquiry.

3- The virtue of the woman who stays secluded in her home, and the blame of the one who goes out often, as Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said.

4- Clarification that the jinn enter Paradise and are made happy therein.

5- Blessing is obtained through "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? i.e., which of His bounties and graces would you deny?

And His saying: ﴿Mudhammatan﴾, i.e., green to the point of blackness, for when the greenness of a thing intensifies it inclines toward black; it is said of them that they are mudhammatan. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? i.e., which of His blessings would you deny, O company of jinn and humankind?

﴿In them﴾, i.e., in the two gardens, ﴿are two gushing springs﴾, i.e., two fountains of water constantly and perpetually. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? i.e., which of His grace and kindness would you deny?

And the saying of the Most Merciful: ﴿In them﴾, i.e., in the two gardens, are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates. The word "fruit" may encompass palm and pomegranate, but the mention of palm and pomegranate is for added excellence, like the mention of the middle prayer after the mention of the five prayers in His saying: ﴿Guard over the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 238]. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ We deny nothing of the favours of our Lord; to You belongs all praise.

And His saying: ﴿In them are good, beautiful women﴾, i.e., in the two gardens are their women, good (khayrat, the plural of khayira), of good character and beautiful faces. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? Would you deny such a bounty and honour upon the friends of the Most Merciful?

﴿Maidens secluded in pavilions﴾: those good women are ḥūr, the plural of ḥawrāʾ, meaning white; a ḥawrāʾ is one in whom the whiteness of the eyes overcomes their blackness, which is a feature of feminine beauty. They are kept within pavilions and look at no one but their husbands. The pavilion is of hollow pearl, sixty miles long, attributed to their palaces.

And His saying: ﴿No man or jinn has touched them before them﴾, i.e., no man or jinn has had intercourse with them, deflowering them, before their husbands in Paradise. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? The answer: we deny nothing of the favours of our Lord; to You belongs all praise.

And His saying: ﴿Reclining on green cushions and beautiful carpets﴾, i.e., reclining on green cushions, the singular of rafraf being rafrafa, that is, on green pillows or carpets, and beautiful carpets, i.e., on rugs with a fine nap. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny: the blessings of this world, or of the barzakh, or of the Hereafter? We deny nothing of the favours of our Lord.

And His saying: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of majesty and honour﴾, i.e., blessed is the name of your Lord: sanctified, and abundant in blessings is the name of your Lord, the Most Merciful, Possessor of majesty, i.e., greatness, and of honour toward His friends and righteous servants.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification that the bliss of the Hereafter is greater and more majestic than the bounties of this world.

2- The excellence of dates and pomegranates, so let us investigate their benefits, for truth is the daughter of inquiry.

3- The virtue of the woman who stays secluded in her home, and the blame of the one who goes out often, as Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said.

4- Clarification that the jinn enter Paradise and are made happy therein.

5- Blessing is obtained through "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."
